metadata.title: 10 ARIA Attributes You'll Use Most in Forms
metadata.subtitle: A Quick Reference
metadata.description: Ten ARIA attributes that come up constantly when building accessible forms — what each one does, and when to reach for it. No fluff, just the reference.

rules.label: aria-label — name a control without visible text
rules.good: Gives icon buttons, search inputs, and other visible-label-less controls an accessible name
rules.bad: Don't use alongside aria-labelledby — if visible text exists, point to it instead

rules.label: aria-labelledby — point to existing visible text as the label
rules.good: Reuses a heading or existing label already in the DOM as the accessible name
rules.bad: Takes an ID (or space-separated IDs), not free text — pointing to the wrong element mislabels the control

rules.label: aria-describedby — link hints and errors to a field
rules.good: Screen reader reads the label first, then the description when the field is focused
rules.bad: Can chain multiple IDs space-separated — forgetting to include both hint and error is a common miss
rules.code:
Must be at least 8 characters.

Password is required.

rules.label: aria-required — mark a field as required
rules.good: Makes sure every screen reader announces the field as required
rules.bad: Relying on the required HTML attribute alone isn't explicit enough in the accessibility tree

rules.label: aria-invalid — mark a field as currently invalid
rules.good: Paired with aria-describedby, tells the screen reader what's wrong, not just that something is
rules.bad: Set to true when validation fails — set back to false, or remove it, once the user fixes it
rules.code: Enter a valid email address.

rules.label: aria-live — announce dynamic content changes
rules.good: polite waits for the user to finish what they're doing; assertive interrupts immediately
rules.bad: Reserve assertive for critical errors only, and mount the live region before the content changes

rules.label: aria-atomic — read the whole live region, not just the changed part
rules.good: The full sentence is announced every time a live region updates, not just the changed node
rules.bad: Without it, a screen reader may only announce the part that changed — like just a number

rules.label: aria-expanded — show open/closed state on a trigger
rules.good: Belongs on the trigger, not the panel — keep it in sync with the visual open/closed state
rules.bad: One of the most common bugs in the wild: state left out of sync with the visible UI
rules.code: {/* filter fields */}

rules.label: aria-controls — link a trigger to what it controls
rules.good: Lets some screen readers jump users directly from the trigger to the controlled region
rules.bad: Support is inconsistent across screen readers — don't rely on it alone, treat it as progressive enhancement
rules.code: {/* options */}

rules.label: aria-hidden — remove decorative content from the accessibility tree
rules.good: Decorative icons, dividers, and duplicate content are skipped by screen readers
rules.bad: Never on a focusable element, and never to hide error messages or instructions users need to act on
rules.code:
<!-- Decorative icon — SR skips it -->
<svg aria-hidden="true" focusable="false">...</svg>

<!-- Label already reads "Search" — hide the redundant icon -->
<button>
  <svg aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><!-- search icon --></svg>
  Search
</button>

checklist.item: aria-label — name a control without visible text
aria-labelledby — point to existing visible text as the label
aria-describedby — link hints and errors to a field
aria-required — mark a field as required
aria-invalid — mark a field as currently invalid
aria-atomic — read the whole live region, not just the changed part
aria-expanded — show open/closed state on a trigger
aria-controls — link a trigger to what it controls
aria-hidden — remove decorative content from the accessibility tree
